mechanism_narrative: A higher monthly FEDFUNDS rate predicts lower S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to tightened discount rates affecting future cash flows.
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero-rate baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment) correlates with stronger consumer demand, which elevates S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 20-day horizon, the correlation between PAYEMS and SPX 5-day returns is <0.2 in absolute value.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (retail sales) followed by a decline in UNRATE (unemployment) signals a turning point toward growth, pushing 60-day SPX forward returns positive.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% in the following month and UNRATE falls by >0.2pp in the same month.
regime_hint: transition from deflationary to growth-oriented labor market
failure_condition: Over 12 such HOUST/UNRATE turning points, cumulative 60-day returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in INDPRO (industrial production) below trend predicts reduced corporate earnings expectations, causing a negative 20-day SPX forward return.
failure_condition: Over 30 such INDPRO contractions, 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative (median < 0).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 4%, the 5-day SPX forward return is negative due to higher real borrowing costs compressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: Over 10 such events, 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in RSAFS (retail sales) accompanied by a decline in UNRATE suggests stronger consumer confidence and labor market flexibility, boosting 20-day SPX returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >8% in a month and UNRATE decreases by >0.1pp in the same month.
failure_condition: Across 15 such RSAFS/UNRATE turning points, 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in GDPC1 (GDP) for three consecutive months predicts a positive 60-day SPX forward return as market anticipates growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 10 such 3-month GDPC1 growth streaks, 60-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) unexpectedly rises by >0.5% in a month, the S&P 20-day forward return is negative due to inflation fears.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% in a given month
failure_condition: Over 8 such CPIAUCSL spikes, 20-day returns are not consistently negative (median > 0).
